children: The Bank of Japan lifted its key short-term rate by 25bps to 1.25% in a 7-2 vote at its September meeting, marking the highest level since April 1995 and aligning with market expectations.
The move came as the central bank sought to address persistent inflationary pressures, including those stemming from higher oil prices.
It marked the first rate hike in three months and another step away from decades of ultra-low interest rates.
Board members Asada Toichiro and Sato Ayano dissented.

title: BoJ Hikes Rate to 31-Year High
